bib.title: Introduction to the CoNLL-2003 Shared Task: Language-Independent Named Entity Recognition

question: How well can sixteen machine-learning systems recognise persons, organizations, locations and miscellaneous names in English and German text, and does extra information (gazetteers, unannotated data) help?
hypothesis: Plainly implied: systems that make use of resources beyond the supplied training data, especially unannotated data, will do better.
contributions: Annotated English and German NER data sets (train/dev/test plus unannotated text) in a four-column IOB format
An F1 evaluation protocol with bootstrap significance bounds
A comparison of sixteen participating systems, their features and use of external resources
A majority-vote combination of the systems as an upper-bound probe

method.summary: Organizers released English (Reuters) and German (Frankfurter Rundschau) news text hand-annotated with PER, ORG, LOC and MISC entities. Sixteen teams trained on the training file, tuned on the development file and were scored once on the test file by exact-match entity F1. The paper surveys the systems, features and external resources, and tests a majority vote over systems.
method.task: named entity recognition (sequence labelling, 4 entity types)

datasets.name: CoNLL-2003 English
datasets.size: train 946 articles / 14,987 sentences / 203,621 tokens; dev 216 / 3,466 / 51,362; test 231 / 3,684 / 46,435
datasets.split: train/dev/test as supplied; dev for tuning, test for comparison
datasets.source: Reuters Corpus, Aug 1996 to Aug 1997 news; train and dev from ten days at end of Aug 1996, test from Dec 1996
datasets.preprocessing: tokenizer, MBT POS tagger and chunker; hand NE tagging at Univ. of Antwerp, mostly MUC conventions plus MISC; IOB tags; non-recursive, non-overlapping, top-level entity only

datasets.name: CoNLL-2003 German
datasets.size: train 553 articles / 12,705 sentences / 206,931 tokens; dev 201 / 3,068 / 51,444; test 155 / 3,160 / 51,943
datasets.source: ECI Multilingual Text Corpus, Frankfurter Rundschau; all three sets from one week at end of Aug 1992
datasets.preprocessing: tokenizer, Treetagger lemma, POS and chunk; hand NE tagging; IOB tags

datasets.name: Unannotated text (English, German)
datasets.source: English: Reuters Sept 1996; German: Sept to Dec 1992

models.name: Sixteen participating systems (Florian, Chieu, Klein, Zhang, Carreras a/b, Curran, Mayfield, McCallum, Bender, Munro, Wu, Whitelaw, Hendrickx, De Meulder, Hammerton)
models.architecture: MaxEnt (5), HMM (4), RRM/Winnow, voted perceptron, LSTM, AdaBoost.MH (2), memory-based (2), TBL, SVM, CRF; 5 used system combination

models.name: Baseline
models.architecture: labels only phrases with a unique class in training data; longest phrase if several

inference.samples: one test-set run per system; 250 bootstrap samples of sentences per output file for significance

parameters.majority_vote_search: bidirectional hill-climbing, beam size 9, over 16 systems, selected on dev data
parameters.significance_rule: A differs from B if A is outside the centre 90% of B's distribution

metrics.name: F(beta=1)
metrics.definition: 2PR/(P+R); precision = % of found entities that are correct, recall = % of corpus entities found; entity correct only on exact match

metrics.name: error reduction
metrics.definition: relative reduction in error on dev data with extra information vs training data only

eval.protocol: Train on train, tune on dev, report once on test; bootstrap resampling (Noreen 1989), 250 samples, 90% centre interval

limits: Only two languages, both European news text; German and English are the sole test of 'language independence'.
Single test-set run per system; no seeds or repeated training reported.
Exact-match F1 only; MISC is a catch-all category the authors call very diverse.
Entities are non-recursive and non-overlapping; nested entities annotated at top level only.
Test sets come from a later period than train/dev (English Dec 1996 vs Aug 1996), so temporal drift is mixed into the test score.
Authors state that how best to exploit raw text remains open; gazetteer and external-NER gains needed much manual work.
Table 4 gives '?' for McCallum and Wu error reductions.
